verdict.rationale: Snowflake's own docs cover bulk operations in several places: bulk copying of data into and out of tables, restoring all objects inside a container at once, and cloning a database or schema together with all its child objects. A community user confirms that COPY loads many files in one pass and skips files already loaded. The evidence does not show a general bulk-action capability for managing many arbitrary items at once, so full story coverage is not established. Missing for 10: documented bulk/batch management of arbitrary objects (e.g. bulk user/role/grant changes via REST API, CLI or MCP), an explicit agent-facing batch execution path, and independent corroboration beyond data loading.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: Bulk copying data into and out of Snowflake tables.
You can restore individual objects, such as tables, or restore all the objects inside a container object
If the source object is a database or schema, the clone inherits all granted privileges on the clones of all child objects contained in the source object
The COPY command will even skip files it has already loaded.
